detail.longDescription: I'm sending HTTPS requests through an authenticated HTTP proxy with the Requests library. The password contains @ and : , which are reserved characters in a URL's userinfo part. import requests from urllib.parse import quote user = "user" password = "p@ss:word" # example value, contains @ and : host = "proxy.example.com:8080" proxy_url = f"http://{quote(user, safe='')}:{quote(password, safe='')}@{host}" proxies = { "http": proxy_url, "https": proxy_url, } r = requests.get("https://httpbin.org/ip", proxies=proxies, timeout=10) print(r.status_code, r.text) The same URL can also be supplied through the environment instead of the proxies argument: export HTTPS_PROXY='http://user:p%40ss%3Aword@proxy.example.com:8080' python script.py My understanding is this: Without encoding, p@ss:word makes the URL ambiguous, because everything after the last @ is read as the host. With quote(password, safe='') , the string becomes p%40ss%3Aword . Requests is supposed to percent-decode the userinfo again before it builds the Proxy-Authorization: Basic ... header for the CONNECT request. I could not find this stated explicitly in the Requests documentation. I only want to rely on it if it is guaranteed behavior and not an accident of the current implementation. When credentials are embedded in a proxy URL passed to Requests (via proxies= or HTTPS_PROXY ), does Requests unquote them before sending Proxy-Authorization , and is urllib.parse.quote(value, safe='') the right way to encode them? I'm also interested in whether the answer differs between the proxies= argument and the environment variables, since both go through different code paths in Session . Environment: Python 3, Requests v2.x, urllib3 v2.x, HTTP proxy that requires Basic authentication.
